item.title: Auto sales cooled in February, dealers say
item.description: Seasonally adjusted auto sales fell to a 15.4 million annual rate as incentives thinned.
item.content:encoded:
Inventory on dealer lots rose for a second month.

$F reported the smallest decline among the large domestic brands, while $TSLA held flat.

item.title: Steel mill restarts a second furnace
item.description: The restart adds about 900,000 tonnes of annual capacity in the region.
item.content:encoded:
The steelmaker said in a statement that the second furnace restarted on schedule and will reach full output by the end of April.

It said the maintenance programme cost 60 million dollars and added 40 permanent jobs at the site.

The plant manager said the older furnace would stay idle until demand improves.

item.title: Mining equipment orders hold steady
item.description: Order books at the largest suppliers were flat against a strong comparison period.
item.content:encoded:
Dealers said Caterpillar took the biggest share of new truck orders.

Analysts said Caterpillar would keep pricing firm through the year.

One dealer said Caterpillar delivery times had shortened to nine months.

Shipments to dealers rose 4 percent on the quarter.

Rebuild work at Caterpillar dealers rose 7 percent, the dealers said.

item.title: Industrial shares climbed as orders improved
item.description: The industrial subindex rose 1.1 percent after a survey showed new orders expanding.
item.content:encoded:
Trading across the sector was heavier than average for a Wednesday.

Premarket moves had pointed the other way.

Among the movers, CAT gained 1.8 percent on volume of 3 million shares.

item.title: Market Minute | Search advertising growth is slowing
item.description: Agencies trimmed their forecasts for paid search after a soft January in retail categories.
item.content:encoded:
Agency forecasts now put category growth in the high single digits for the full year, down from the low teens estimated in the autumn.

Buyers said Alphabet had held its share of that spending through the slowdown.

Analysts said Alphabet would lean on retail media to defend growth.

One agency said Alphabet offered better terms on annual commitments.

The annual budget is now split between search and retail media.

Budgets committed to Alphabet rose 2 percent in the quarter, the agency said.

Figures are indicative only.

item.title: Grocery pricing pressure squeezes margins
item.description: Supermarket chains cut list prices on staples for a second quarter running.
item.content:encoded:
Suppliers said Target had pushed hardest on private-label pricing this year.

Analysts said Target would protect trips rather than basket size.

One supplier said Target asked for longer payment terms.

Chains said holiday volumes had already normalised, and one retailer trimmed its forecast for the spring.

Shelf space at Target for national brands narrowed again, suppliers said.

item.title: Market Minute | For long-stay travellers, Visa fees rose
item.description: The consulate said the new schedule applies to applications filed after April 1.
item.content:encoded:
Tourists booking Amazon river cruises need the same documents, the consulate said.

Applications from students will be processed under the old fee, the embassy said.

Figures are indicative only.

item.title: Price target cuts pile up across software
item.description: Three banks trimmed their price targets after a weak quarter, citing slower seat growth.
item.content:encoded:
Analysts kept their ratings unchanged even as estimates came down.

The average price target across the group fell 9 percent.

item.title: Allstate raises home premiums after a costly storm season
item.description: The Allstate Corporation (NYSE: ALL) said it would raise home premiums in four states after a costly storm season.
item.content:encoded:
Policyholders will see the change at renewal.

Claims from the season exceeded the company's reinsurance attachment point.

item.title: Market Minute | Upgrade cycles for smartphones keep lengthening
item.description: Two carriers said the average replacement cycle has passed four years in their largest markets.
item.content:encoded:
Carriers said Apple has stretched that cycle furthest, trimming quarterly sales of new handsets.

Analysts at two firms said Apple would offset the slowdown with services revenue.

One supplier said Apple accounted for a fifth of its shipments last year.

Rivals have not matched Apple on trade pricing, the carriers said.

The hardware still sells at a premium in that market.

Figures are indicative only.

item.title: Target audiences are fragmenting, marketers say
item.description: Planners said reach is harder to buy as viewing spreads across more channels.
item.content:encoded:
The demographic once bought in a single campaign is now split across four.

Agencies said measurement lags the shift.

item.title: Premarket movers across software, energy and insurance
item.description: Analysts said margins held up better than feared across the sector as freight costs eased again.
item.content:encoded:
Volume in the premarket session was thin and few of the moves held into the open.

Among the movers, $ORCL, $SHEL and $GOOGL rose, while $META, $CAT and $ALL slipped.

item.title: Across the valley, Apple growers brace for frost
item.description: Growers said an early frost damaged blossom across the valley and the harvest may fall by a fifth.
item.content:encoded:
Growers said Apple futures on the produce exchange rose 6 percent as buyers weighed a smaller crop.

Orchard owners have hired fewer seasonal workers than last year.

Caterpillar damage in the same orchards was lighter than last season.

The cooperative said cider makers and pie bakers would feel the shortage first.

Buyers said the fruit suits a pie recipe rather than pressing.

Figures are indicative only.

item.title: Five habits that save time in Shell scripting for beginners
item.description: The tutorial covers quoting, exit codes and how to keep a script readable.
item.content:encoded:
Bind the Meta key before you start, the tutorial says.

Scripts in the examples avoid subshells where a repeat will do.

Figures are indicative only.

item.title: The deposit war spreads to smaller lenders
item.description: Two rivals matched the offer within a day, and one fund manager said the offer was priced to move.
item.content:encoded:
The bank said in a statement that the new rate applies to balances above 5,000 dollars and takes effect on the first of the month.

It said branch staffing would not change, and that the decision followed a review of funding costs.

The chief financial officer said the move should protect the deposit base without hurting margin.

item.title: Pickup incentives return to the market
item.description: Average incentives on full-size pickups reached 6 percent of sticker price last month.
item.content:encoded:
Dealers said Ford moved first with cash back on its most popular trims.

Analysts said Ford would defend share rather than margin this year.

One dealer said Ford inventory had climbed for a third month.

Production of the smaller pickup was unaffected, the dealers said.

Buyers cross-shopping Ford took longer to close, the dealers said.

item.title: Caterpillar books a record backlog as dealers restock
item.description: Caterpillar Inc. (NYSE: CAT) said its order backlog reached a record as dealers restocked excavators before the construction season.
item.content:encoded:
Sales of construction equipment rose 9 percent in the quarter.

The company kept its full-year outlook unchanged.

item.title: Insurers led the market higher on Tuesday
item.description: The insurance subindex rose 1.4 percent, the strongest showing among financial groups.
item.content:encoded:
Volume across the sector was above its ten-day average for a third session.

The index closed higher as investors weighed interest rates, and turnover on the exchange was heavy.

Among the largest names, ALL rose 2.1 percent on volume of 4 million shares.

item.title: Meta-analysis says statin benefit was overstated
item.description: The systematic review pooled 42 randomized trials and found a smaller effect on heart attacks than earlier estimates.
item.content:encoded:
Patients in the control groups had similar readings at baseline.

Patients had a CAT scan at an imaging clinic in 14 of the pooled trials.

The authors said the journal will publish the full cohort data in June.

Figures are indicative only.
